questions.questionText: Which statement about factors of production is correct?

options.text: Capital is the amount of money borrowed from a bank.
Labour is output made by an employee.
Land includes commercially grown rice crops.
Profit is the reward for enterprise.

questions.questionText:
Sam wrote a list of how he would prefer to spend his Saturday afternoon.
first choice go to a cricket match
second choice watch the annual town parade
third choice go to the cinema
fourth choice visit relatives
Unfortunately a thunderstorm caused the cricket match and the town parade to be cancelled.
Sam went to the cinema.
What was the opportunity cost of going to the cinema?

What suggests that there is market failure?
What can cause the supply curve for a product to shift to the right?

options.text: an increase in demand for the product
an increase in government subsidies to producers
an increase in indirect taxes on the product
an increase in the costs of production

questions.questionText:
A railway company increases ticket prices by 10% for travel between 06:00 and 09:00, causing a
reduction in demand by 2%. After 09:00 it reduces ticket prices by 5%, resulting in a 7% increase
in demand.
What is the price elasticity of demand in response to these price changes?
between 06:00
after 09:00
and 09:00
What is a disadvantage of being a specialist skilled worker?

options.text: Earnings are related to the level of skill.
It may be difficult to find work locally.
Labour supply is elastic and plentiful.

questions.questionText: What is not normally a function of the central bank of a country?

options.text: acting as lender of last resort

Why are indirect taxes, such as VAT of 20% on goods and services, described as regressive
when comparing high-income and low-income purchasers?

options.text: High-income purchasers pay a higher percentage of their income in tax.
High-income purchasers pay a lower percentage of their income in tax.
Low-income purchasers pay a lower percentage of their income in tax.
Low-income purchasers and high-income purchasers pay the same percentage of their income in tax.

questions.questionText:
The government has an important role in mixed economies.
Which function would it not perform?

options.text: distributing dividends from profits of state-owned enterprises

questions.questionText: Which combination of policy measures would be effective in reducing the effects of a recession?

options.text: a reduction in interest rates and a reduction in income tax
a reduction in interest rates and an increase in income tax
an increase in interest rates and a reduction in income tax
an increase in interest rates and an increase in income tax

fiscal monetary supply-side
policy policy policy

Why was the Human Development Index (HDI) introduced as a measure of the standard of
living?

options.text: Education and healthcare are important contributors to the standard of living.
GDP per head only measures development.
Inequality can only be measured by HDI.
Literacy rates are not an effective measure of the standard of living.

questions.questionText:
During periods of high unemployment across the entire labour force, the highest unemployment
rate in an economy is often in the 16–19 year-old age group.
Which statement explains why 16–19 year-olds may find it difficult to find a job?

options.text: The incentive to earn an income is lower for that age group.
Their wages are lower than those of adults.
They lack both work experience and the necessary skills.
They prefer leisure activities to long working hours.

questions.questionText:
Venezuela, a leading world oil producer, has experienced hyperinflation of over 400% per annum
in recent years.
How does hyperinflation affect an economy?
prices effect

options.text: fluctuate up and down consumers are uncertain about future price levels
fluctuate up and down consumers can anticipate future price levels
rise very rapidly value of fixed assets remains stable
rise very rapidly money has limited worth as a medium of exchange

questions.questionText: What is most likely to increase as a country becomes more developed?

options.text: the proportion of income spent on food

questions.questionText:
In Botswana, better healthcare has meant that birth rates have been falling faster than death
rates. Also the number of children born, on average, to each woman has declined from 6.4 to 3.2.
What may be concluded from this information?

options.text: Government spending on education will need to increase.
Medical improvements have resulted in falling infant mortality rates.
There will be a decline in income for each person working.
There will, in the long run, be an increase in the working population.

questions.questionText:
The table shows the percentage share of GDP held by the richest 20% and poorest 20% of the
population in each country.
Which country had the greatest extremes of income and poverty?
country richest 20% poorest 20%
What would cause a favourable change in the Kenyan trade in services (invisible) account?

options.text: A Kenyan company wins a contract to transport exports from Uganda.
A Kenyan tea company increases its exports.
A Kenyan trade delegation promoting coffee sales visits India.
A Zambian company increases its exports to Kenya.

questions.questionText: What is a disadvantage of trade protection of manufactured goods?

options.text: It can lead to retaliation from trading partners.
It encourages infant industries to grow.
It increases demand for domestic manufactured goods.
It reduces outflows of currencies to pay for imports.

questions.questionText: What would cause a rise in the deficit on the current account of the balance of payments?

options.text: a fall in foreign direct investment into the country
a fall in interest earned on overseas investment by the country
a fall in the value of imported manufactured goods into the country
a rise in the revenue earned from tourism in the country
